title: Type hints and dataclasses

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?

Modern annotations express contracts such as `list[str]`, `str | None`, `TypedDict`, and `Protocol`; Python does not enforce them during ordinary execution. Static checkers such as Pyright or mypy analyze these contracts. `Protocol` describes required behavior without forcing inheritance, while `TypedDict` describes expected dictionary keys. Validate external data separately with a runtime validator such as Pydantic.

CORE EXPLANATION
Type hints communicate expected values to readers and static tools; Python does not enforce them during ordinary execution. dataclass reduces boilerplate for simple data objects.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Never log passwords, tokens, or personal data; a type hint is not runtime validation.
COMMON MISTAKES
Keep tests deterministic and make log levels and type contracts explicit.
